newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin aide under attack over arming Cossacks.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin aide under attack over arming Cossacks.

text.p: A Kremlin aide under fire in the upper house of parliament shrugged off calls to force him out of office on Thursday and said only President Boris Yeltsin could sack him.

Businessman Boris Berezovsky, criticised by parliament for suggesting that Cossacks in southern Russia should be allowed to bear arms in self-defence, told Ekho Moskvy radio that the suggestion was senseless.
"It is for the president to decide," he said.
Interfax news agency had said the Federation Council had urged Yeltsin to sack Berezovsky, but it later said the demand had been withdrawn from a final version of the resolution.

"If we arm the civilian population, there could without a doubt be a second Caucasus war and the Federation Council is decisively against that, but not against individuals," Interfax quoted council head Yegor Stroyev as saying.

The Cossacks, decendants of pioneers planted by Russia on its southern fringes in the 16th century to protect borders and win new lands for the empire, say they need arms to secure their lands from Chechen separatists.
Their leaders say a peace deal under which Russia withdrew troops from Chechnya was humiliating for Russia and showed the government was not capable of defending its territory.

They say the withdrawal left southern Russian regions exposed to Chechen attacks. They also demand that some parts in Northern Chechnya, which they view as traditional Cossack domains, be taken back by force if Chechnya secedes.

Berezovsky, ordered by Yeltsin to oversee the Chechnya settlement, was shown on television as telling the Cossacks that he backed their demands and that he would leave Yeltsin's administration if it does not support the idea of arming them.
Many political and regional leaders, who see Cossacks as a conservative military force which Moscow used in the past to impose its will, view arming them as a threat to stability.
Berezovsky was the second top Kremlin aide to come under parliamentary attack.
The State Duma lower house earlier this week urged Yeltsin to sack his liberal chief of staff Anatoly Chubais.
There was no immediate reaction from the Kremlin to the Federation Council's appeal.
